name: Riluzole
route_note: Oral tablet twice daily; also oral suspension and oral film for people with swallowing difficulty.

discovery.note: A benzothiazole studied as an anticonvulsant and neuroprotectant before being tested in ALS on the glutamate excitotoxicity hypothesis.

tagline: The first drug shown to prolong survival in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
summary: Riluzole was the first medicine approved for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). It modestly prolongs survival or time to tracheostomy, by roughly two to three months in pivotal trials.
mechanism: Riluzole inhibits presynaptic glutamate release, blocks voltage-gated sodium channels (particularly the persistent sodium current) and non-competitively affects some postsynaptic glutamate receptor responses.
These actions are thought to reduce glutamate-mediated excitotoxic injury to motor neurons, though the precise mechanism in ALS is not fully defined.

history.title: First trial
history.detail: Bensimon et al. (NEJM) report improved survival in ALS with riluzole.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Rilutek becomes the first FDA-approved ALS drug in December.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Rilutek is authorised in the European Union.

history.title: Edaravone
history.detail: The FDA approves edaravone (Radicava), the second drug for ALS, more than 20 years after riluzole.

history.title: Oral suspension
history.detail: Tiglutik thickened oral suspension is approved in the US.

history.title: Oral film
history.detail: Exservan, an oral soluble film, is approved in the US.

facts: The survival benefit of riluzole in its pivotal trials was modest, but it remained the only approved ALS drug for more than two decades.
